context_requirements: Cells must have active iron/heavy-metal homeostasis and metal-responsive transcription (MTF1, HIF1, NRF2) to show early metal-stress genes.
Cells must have active sterol/cholesterol biosynthesis for the early down-regulation of HMGCR and related genes.
Cells with high basal oxidative stress or defective NRF2 may show weaker HMOX1/MT induction.
Hepatocyte-like lines (HEPG2) with strong metal and xenobiotic handling may respond more strongly.
falsifiers: No early (6 h) induction of HMOX1, MT1X, MT2A, or SLC11A2 in any of the nine lines.
No early (6 h) down-regulation of HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1, or other cholesterol-synthesis genes.
A purely late (24 h) response with no 6 h changes, which would argue against direct metal chelation as the primary mechanism.
Strong induction of interferon or heat-shock programs instead of metal/oxidative-stress programs.
No difference in response between lines with intact versus defective metal-responsive transcription.
